title: Residue field extensions of a finite type ring map are finitely generated
statement: Let $f:R\to R'$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings of finite type, i.e. $R'$ is generated as an $R$-algebra by finitely many elements $x_1,\dots,x_n$. Let $\mathfrak p'\subset R'$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak p=f^{-1}(\mathfrak p')$, a prime ideal of $R$, and let $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$, $\kappa(\mathfrak p')=R'_{\mathfrak p'}/\mathfrak p'R'_{\mathfrak p'}$ be the residue fields [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], with the ring map $\bar f:\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ induced by $f$ (the class of $a/s$, $a\in R$, $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$, goes to the class of $f(a)/f(s)$). Then $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$, a field extension of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ through $\bar f$ [def-pc-field-extension], is finitely generated: there are finitely many $a_1,\dots,a_m\in\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ such that $\kappa(\mathfrak p')=\kappa(\mathfrak p)(a_1,\dots,a_m)$, the smallest subfield of $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ containing $\bar f(\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ and $a_1,\dots,a_m$.
